description: A state-variable filter with lowpass, bandpass, highpass and notch outputs at once, a trigger input for striking it, and enough resonance to ring on its own

params.text: Scales the signal input, from silence to the whole of it
Sets the filter frequency, an octave a step from 0.0625Hz to 8192Hz
Sets the resonance; near the top the filter rings and the outputs can reach 12V either way, so raise it a little at a time
Scales the FREQ control input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the frequency
Scales the RES control input, -2 to +2, before it is added to the resonance

inputs.text: Strikes the filter on each rise past 1.8V by sending a short 6V pulse through it, which rings the filter like a struck object
Added to the filter frequency with no attenuation of its own, a volt an octave
Added to the filter frequency through its attenuverter, a volt an octave
Added to the resonance through its attenuverter
The signal to be filtered, scaled by its attenuator; audio and slow control voltages both work

notes: the input attenuator starts fully down, so a fresh module passes nothing until it is turned up
patch BAND back into IN and raise the input attenuator and the resonance until it sings, and the four outputs give the same sine wave a quarter cycle apart
at high resonance the outputs can reach 24V peak to peak, which is far above what most modules expect, so bring the resonance up gradually
every input in this module reads one channel, so polyphonic cables are cut down to their first channel

inputs.0:
high above 1.8V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 1V per octave.
